rationale: Round 0 compiled, ran correctly, and hit no ICE fallback, so this round shifts the table toward stronger obfuscation while keeping cost sensitivity moderate enough to stay safe. SUB and SPLIT get the most permissive profile (high security/diversity weights, very low cost weights) since instruction substitution and basic-block splitting are cheap, correctness-safe transformations that add diversity across all 26 functions of this small 4.3 KB C++ OOP benchmark. FLA and BCF are the primary resistance sources for the few meaty functions (main at 1017 bytes, rectangle::draw at 811 bytes), so their SecurityGain stays highest but their SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights are raised above round 0 to keep text growth proportionate on a program where the largest function is only ~1 KB; BCF is kept slightly more size-constrained than FLA since bogus control flow inflates size fastest. IBR and ICALL get strong weights — indirect branching and indirect calls are especially disruptive to static analysis of the virtual-call-heavy draw() hierarchies here — with moderate cost weights to bound dispatch overhead. IGV remains the most constrained pass: its global-variable encoding interacts with the C++ constructors (myshape, rectangle initialization) where correctness risk concentrates, so its CorrectnessRisk and SizeCost weights stay the highest in the table, letting it apply only where features strongly favor it.
